q: Which type of law covers legally enforceable agreements between two or more parties?
r: Contract law
Contract law governs agreements that courts will enforce.
w: Criminal law
Criminal law punishes offences against the public, not private agreements.
Tort law
Tort law covers civil wrongs that cause harm, such as negligence.
Constitutional law
Constitutional law defines government powers and individual rights.

q: Sol's Sandwich Shack registers the name of its signature sandwich so rivals cannot sell something confusingly similar under that name. Which protection did Sol's most likely use?
r: Trademark
A trademark protects names, logos and slogans that identify a business's goods.
w: Patent
A patent protects new inventions, not brand names.
Copyright
Copyright protects original creative works such as writing or art.
Franchise agreement
A franchise agreement licenses a business model; it does not stop others copying a name.

q: A customer slips on a freshly mopped floor in a store that put out no warning sign. The customer's claim that the store failed to take reasonable care is based on which concept?
r: Negligence
Negligence is failing to use the care a reasonable person would, causing harm to someone.
w: Fraud
Fraud requires intentional deception, which is not described here.
Defamation
Defamation involves false statements that harm a reputation.
Breach of warranty
A warranty claim concerns goods that fail a promise about quality.

q: Dana, who is 15, signs a contract to buy a used scooter on credit. Which statement is generally true?
r: Dana can usually cancel the contract, because minors may void most contracts
The law protects minors by letting them cancel most contracts, apart from necessities.
w: The contract is fully binding because Dana signed it
A signature does not remove a minor's right to cancel most contracts.
The contract is void only if the seller agrees to cancel it
A minor's right to cancel does not depend on the seller's consent.
Dana loses the right to cancel after one day
Minors may generally cancel for a reasonable time, so a one-day limit is not the rule.

q: What is the purpose of a statute of limitations?
r: To set a deadline for filing a lawsuit
After the deadline passes, a court will usually refuse to hear the claim.
w: To cap how much a court can award in damages
Caps on damages are separate rules.
To list which crimes count as felonies
Classifying crimes is the job of criminal statutes.
To require certain contracts to be in writing
That rule is the statute of frauds.

q: In the communication process, which element is the person who creates and sends the message?
r: Sender
The sender encodes the idea and transmits it.
w: Receiver
The receiver is the person who gets and interprets the message.
Channel
The channel is the medium that carries the message.
Feedback
Feedback is the receiver's response back to the sender.

q: A manager emails a 400-word update to a team that only needs to know a meeting moved to 3 p.m. Which communication principle did the manager ignore?
r: Conciseness
Conciseness means using only the words needed to get the point across.
w: Courtesy
Nothing in the email was impolite.
Correctness
The facts may be right; the problem is length.
Completeness
The email had far more than enough detail.

q: During a live presentation, a speaker avoids eye contact and talks in a flat, quiet voice. Which area of communication is the main weakness?
r: Delivery and nonverbal communication
Eye contact and vocal variety are nonverbal skills that shape how a message lands.
w: Word choice
The scenario says nothing about vocabulary.
Accuracy of the information
The facts are not in question here.
Document formatting
A live talk has no document to format.

q: A team member says, 'I hear that the deadline is worrying you. Let's look at what is realistic.' Which skill is being shown?
r: Active listening
Restating the concern shows the speaker understood it before responding.
w: Persuasive selling
Nothing is being sold or pitched.
Delegating
No task is being handed to anyone.
Proofreading
Proofreading checks written text for errors.

q: Which is the best way to share one employee's confidential salary details?
r: A private one-on-one meeting
Only the employee hears the information.
w: A company-wide chat channel
Everyone in the channel could read it.
A notice on the break room board
Anyone passing by could read it.
A group text to the whole team
Every member of the group would see it.

q: Which action is an example of customer service after a sale?
r: Following up to check the customer is satisfied
A follow-up shows the business cares about the result and invites feedback.
w: Raising prices for repeat buyers
This does nothing to support the customer after the sale.
Closing the store early on weekends
Hours of operation are not service after a sale.
Removing the return policy from the website
Hiding the policy makes post-sale service worse.

q: A customer brings back a blender with a cracked lid seven days after buying it. Which response best builds goodwill?
r: Apologize, check the return policy, and offer a replacement or refund
This solves the problem quickly and keeps the customer's trust.
w: Say that cracked lids are normal wear
Dismissing the complaint damages trust.
Ask for a written complaint before helping
Extra steps frustrate a customer with a valid issue.
Suggest buying a second blender at a discount
This ignores the original defect.

q: Which measure best shows how many customers keep buying from a business over time?
r: Customer retention rate
Retention rate compares customers kept to customers at the start of a period.
w: Gross margin
Gross margin shows profit on sales, not customer loyalty.
Inventory turnover
This shows how quickly stock sells.
Break-even point
This shows the sales needed to cover costs.

q: A customer calls in angry about a late order. What should the representative do first?
r: Listen without interrupting and acknowledge the concern
Letting the customer be heard calms the situation and clarifies the problem.
w: Explain company shipping policy in detail
Policy talk before listening feels dismissive.
Transfer the call to a supervisor
Passing the call along without trying to help adds frustration.
Offer a discount before hearing the problem
A discount may not address what actually went wrong.

q: Which person is an external customer of a shoe store?
r: A shopper buying running shoes
External customers are people outside the business who buy its products.
w: A cashier employed by the store
Employees are inside the business.
A stockroom worker who unpacks deliveries
This is also an employee, so an internal role.
A store manager reviewing sales reports
Managers are part of the business.

q: When the price of a product rises and everything else stays the same, what usually happens to the quantity demanded?
r: It falls
The law of demand says higher prices reduce the quantity buyers want.
w: It rises
That would go against the law of demand.
It stays exactly the same
Buyers normally respond to price changes.
It doubles
Nothing in the law of demand supports such a jump.

q: Which good is the best example of a substitute for tea?
r: Coffee
Consumers may switch to coffee when tea gets more expensive.
w: Honey
Honey is often used with tea, so it is a complement.
Teapots
Teapots are used together with tea, so they are a complement.
Tea bags
Tea bags are a form of tea, not an alternative to it.

q: Mia can work a Saturday shift that pays $80 or attend a free workshop. She attends the workshop. What is her opportunity cost?
r: The $80 she gave up
Opportunity cost is the value of the next-best alternative given up.
w: The workshop fee
The workshop is free, and fees are not the idea being tested.
Nothing, since she never received the $80
Giving up earnings is still a cost.
The value of every other possible Saturday activity
Only the single best alternative counts.

q: Prices across the economy rise by 4 percent over a year while a worker's wages stay the same. What happens to the worker's purchasing power?
r: It falls
The same wages buy fewer goods and services than before.
w: It rises
Higher prices with flat wages reduce what money can buy.
It stays the same
Purchasing power changes when prices change and income does not.
It doubles
Nothing in the situation could double it.

q: Which item would be counted in this year's gross domestic product (GDP) of the country where it was made?
r: A new bicycle produced and sold by a local manufacturer this year
GDP counts the value of new final goods and services produced in a period.
w: A used bicycle resold between two neighbors
Used goods were counted in GDP when first produced.
Shares of stock bought on an exchange
Buying shares transfers ownership but does not create output.
A government pension payment
Transfer payments are not payment for current production.

q: Which term describes recognizing and managing your own emotions and understanding the emotions of others?
r: Emotional intelligence
It combines self-awareness, self-management and awareness of others.
w: Technical competence
This refers to job-specific skills.
Cognitive bias
A cognitive bias is a pattern of flawed thinking.
Market research
Market research studies customers and competitors.

q: Before replying to a harsh email, Kai takes a short walk to cool down. Which skill is Kai using?
r: Self-regulation
Kai is managing a strong emotion before acting on it.
w: Empathy
Empathy means understanding someone else's feelings.
Procrastination
Kai plans to reply, so this is not avoidance.
Delegation
No work is being handed to another person.

q: A coworker is quiet after receiving criticism in a meeting. Which response best shows empathy?
r: Ask privately how they are doing and listen
This acknowledges their feelings without putting them on the spot.
w: Tell them criticism is part of every job
This dismisses how they feel.
Joke about it to lighten the mood in front of the team
Public jokes can embarrass them further.
Ignore it so they do not feel singled out
Ignoring the situation offers no support.

q: Which is the best example of self-awareness at work?
r: Noticing that tight deadlines make you short-tempered and planning around it
Self-awareness means understanding your own triggers and acting on them.
w: Blaming teammates when a deadline is missed
Blaming others avoids looking at your own behaviour.
Hiding a mistake so the team stays confident
Hiding errors is the opposite of honest self-reflection.
Copying the habits of the most confident teammate
Copying others is not the same as understanding yourself.

q: Which behaviour best shows a positive attitude at work?
r: Looking for solutions when a problem appears
A positive attitude focuses on what can be done.
w: Avoiding tasks that look difficult
Avoidance does not solve problems.
Complaining about every change
Constant complaints drain team morale.
Waiting to be told what to do next
A positive attitude includes taking initiative.

q: Which person starts a business and accepts the financial risk for its success?
r: Entrepreneur
Entrepreneurs organize a business and take on its risk in hope of profit.
w: Consumer
Consumers buy goods and services.
Wholesaler
A wholesaler sells in bulk to other businesses.
Auditor
An auditor reviews financial records.

q: Priya runs a tutoring business alone and is personally responsible for all of its debts. Which form of ownership is this?
r: Sole proprietorship
One owner with no legal separation between the owner and the business.
w: Corporation
A corporation is a separate legal entity with limited liability.
Limited liability company
An LLC protects owners from personal liability for business debts.
Cooperative
A cooperative is owned and run by its members.

q: Which part of a business plan describes the target market, the competition and the customers?
r: Market analysis
This section shows who will buy and who else is selling.
w: Executive summary
This is a short overview of the entire plan.
Financial projections
These estimate future revenue, costs and profit.
Operations plan
This explains how the business will run day to day.

q: Two friends open a bike repair shop. They want their personal assets protected from business debts without the formal rules of a corporation. Which structure fits best?
r: Limited liability company
An LLC combines liability protection with simpler management.
w: General partnership
Partners are personally liable for the business's debts.
Sole proprietorship
This allows only one owner and gives no liability protection.
C corporation
This gives protection but brings stricter formalities and double taxation.

q: What is the name for the money needed to launch a new business?
r: Startup capital
Startup capital pays for the costs of getting a business going.
w: Net income
Net income is profit after expenses.
Accounts receivable
This is money customers owe the business.
Retained earnings
These are profits kept in a business after payouts.

q: Which financial statement reports revenue, expenses and net income for a period of time?
r: Income statement
It shows how much profit or loss a business made over the period.
w: Balance sheet
The balance sheet shows assets, liabilities and equity on one date.
Cash flow statement
This tracks cash moving in and out.
Budget
A budget is a plan for future income and spending.

q: Bright Bean Cafe had $90,000 in sales and $36,000 in cost of goods sold. What is its gross profit?
r: Gross profit equals sales minus cost of goods sold: 90,000 - 36,000.
w: That is the cost of goods sold, not the gross profit.
That adds the two figures instead of subtracting.
The figures do not produce this amount.

q: A business has $50,000 in current assets and $25,000 in current liabilities. What is its current ratio?
r: Current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities: 50,000 / 25,000.
w: This divides the figures the wrong way round.
This is working capital, not a ratio.
Adding the two figures does not give a ratio.

q: Net income was $18,000 on sales of $240,000. What is the net profit margin?
r: 7.5 percent
Net profit margin is net income divided by sales: 18,000 / 240,000.
w: 13.3 percent
This divides sales by net income instead.
75 percent
This misplaces the decimal point.
18 percent
This treats the dollar figure as a percentage.

q: Which type of cost stays the same no matter how many units a business produces?
r: Fixed cost
Rent is a typical fixed cost that does not change with output.
w: Variable cost
Variable costs rise and fall with output.
Marginal cost
Marginal cost is the cost of producing one more unit.
Sunk revenue
This is not a standard cost term.

q: What is the process of finding and attracting qualified candidates for a job?
r: Recruitment
Recruiting builds a pool of applicants for open positions.
w: Orientation
Orientation welcomes people who are already hired.
Appraisal
An appraisal evaluates an employee's performance.
Termination
Termination ends employment.

q: Which HR document lists a position's duties, responsibilities and reporting relationship?
r: Job description
It tells applicants and employees what the role involves.
w: Resume
A resume summarizes a candidate's background.
Performance appraisal
This evaluates how well an employee did the job.
Employee handbook
This covers company-wide policies, not one job.

q: Which U.S. law prohibits employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex or national origin?
r: Title VII of the Civil Rights Act
Title VII bars these forms of discrimination in hiring and employment.
w: Fair Labor Standards Act
This law covers minimum wage, overtime and child labor.
Family and Medical Leave Act
This law provides job-protected leave for certain reasons.
Occupational Safety and Health Act
This law sets workplace safety standards.

q: A supervisor gives a new hire written feedback every 90 days, measured against agreed goals. This process is best called:
r: Performance appraisal
An appraisal compares an employee's performance with set standards.
w: Job analysis
Job analysis studies what a position requires.
Onboarding
Onboarding is the introduction to the company and role.
Exit interview
An exit interview happens when someone leaves.

q: Which benefit is an example of non-monetary compensation?
r: A flexible work schedule
Flexibility has value to an employee without being a cash payment.
w: An hourly wage
Wages are paid in money.
An annual bonus
Bonuses are cash payments.
Overtime pay
Overtime is paid in money.

q: What do we call raw facts and figures before they have been organized or analyzed?
r: Data
Data becomes information once it is organized and given meaning.
w: Information
Information is data that has been processed to be useful.
Software
Software is a set of instructions for a computer.
Hardware
Hardware is the physical equipment.

q: A shop stores customer names, orders and addresses in one organized, searchable electronic system. What is this system called?
r: A database
A database stores structured records that can be searched and updated.
w: A firewall
A firewall blocks unwanted network traffic.
A router
A router directs traffic between networks.
An operating system
This manages a computer's hardware and programs.

q: Which practice best protects customer data held by a business?
r: Limiting access by job role and using strong passwords
Restricting access and using strong credentials reduces the chance of misuse.
w: Sharing one login among all staff
Shared logins make it impossible to track who did what.
Emailing customer files to personal accounts for convenience
This sends sensitive data outside the company's control.
Keeping the files on an open public network drive
Anyone could reach them.

q: A company wants to find which products sell best by region and season. Which tool is best for turning raw sales data into trends?
r: Data analysis software such as a pivot table
Analysis tools summarize large data sets so patterns become clear.
w: A word processor
A word processor is built for writing documents.
An email client
An email client sends and receives messages.
A slide design template
A template controls how slides look, not how data is analyzed.

q: What does regularly backing up data protect against?
r: Loss of data from failure, error or attack
A backup lets a business restore its files.
w: Slow internet speeds
Backups do not change connection speed.
Customer complaints
Backups do not address service issues.
Rising supplier prices
Backups have no effect on prices.

q: Which of the four Ps describes where and how customers can buy a product?
r: Place
Place covers distribution: the locations and channels that make a product available.
w: Product
Product covers what is being sold.
Price
Price covers what customers pay.
Promotion
Promotion covers how customers learn about the product.

q: A company divides its market into groups by age, income and lifestyle. This is called:
r: Market segmentation
Segmentation splits a broad market into groups with similar traits.
w: Product positioning
Positioning is the image a product holds in customers' minds.
Cost-plus pricing
This sets prices by adding a markup to cost.
Brand extension
This applies an existing brand to a new product.

q: Which of these is a need rather than a want for a person living in a cold climate?
r: A winter coat
Protection from cold is a basic requirement.
w: Designer sunglasses
These are a want.
The newest smartphone
A phone upgrade is a want.
Concert tickets
Entertainment is a want.

q: A fictional drink brand stops advertising discounts and starts stressing its recyclable bottle and locally sourced ingredients. This change is mainly a shift in:
r: Positioning
The brand is changing the image it wants customers to hold.
w: Distribution
Distribution is about where the product is sold.
Cost structure
Nothing here describes the brand's costs.
Credit terms
Credit terms cover payment arrangements.

q: A company's logo and slogan are mainly part of its:
r: Brand identity
Brand identity is the set of visible elements that identify a company.
w: Distribution plan
This covers how goods reach customers.
Credit policy
This covers how a business lends to customers.
Break-even analysis
This calculates the sales needed to cover costs.

q: Which operations term describes a product meeting set standards and customer expectations?
r: Quality
Quality means the product is fit for its purpose and consistently meets standards.
w: Capacity
Capacity is how much a business can produce.
Liability
Liability is a legal responsibility or debt.
Margin
Margin is the difference between price and cost.

q: A bakery bakes bread only when orders arrive, to avoid waste and storage costs. This approach is closest to:
r: Just-in-time production
Just-in-time produces goods only as they are needed.
w: Safety stock
Safety stock is extra inventory held as a buffer.
Overstocking
Holding too much inventory is the opposite approach.
Batch hoarding
This is not a recognized production method.

q: Which step most directly lowers the chance of a workplace injury?
r: Training employees to use equipment safely
Training builds safe habits and prevents misuse of machines.
w: Raising production quotas
Higher pressure can increase risk.
Shortening employee breaks
Tired workers are more likely to make mistakes.
Moving machines closer together
Less space can make accidents more likely.

q: A cafe's espresso station can serve 40 customers an hour, but 60 customers arrive each hour at the lunch peak. What is the most likely result?
r: A line forms and wait times grow
Demand above capacity creates a backlog.
w: Wait times fall
Demand above capacity makes waits longer.
Capacity rises automatically
Capacity stays the same unless the business changes something.
Output increases to 60 an hour
The station cannot produce beyond its capacity.

q: What is a supplier?
r: A business that provides goods or services to another business
Suppliers are the source of materials a business uses or resells.
w: A person who buys a finished product
That describes a customer.
A business that sells similar products in the same market
That describes a competitor.
A government agency that enforces rules
That describes a regulator.

q: What do we call a written set of career goals along with the steps to reach them?
r: Career plan
A career plan links goals to specific actions and timelines.
w: Business plan
A business plan describes how a company will operate.
Expense report
An expense report lists spending.
Job offer
A job offer is an employer's proposal of employment.

q: Which action best builds a professional network?
r: Attending industry events and following up with the people you meet
Staying in touch turns introductions into real relationships.
w: Posting only about yourself online
Networking is two-way, so this does not build relationships.
Waiting for contacts to approach you
Networking needs initiative.
Collecting business cards without contacting anyone
Contacts only matter if you follow up.

q: How should a professional best respond to constructive criticism from a manager?
r: Listen, ask questions and apply useful suggestions
This shows maturity and a willingness to improve.
w: Defend every decision right away
Defensiveness blocks learning.
Point out the mistakes of other coworkers
This shifts attention without improving anything.
Avoid the manager afterward
Avoidance damages the working relationship.

q: A student wants to show employers real evidence of design and writing skills. Which item is most effective?
r: A portfolio of work samples
Samples of actual work prove what the person can do.
w: A longer list of hobbies
Hobbies do not demonstrate job skills.
A cover letter with no examples
Claims without evidence are weak proof of skill.
A list of favorite classes
Favorites say little about ability.

q: Arriving on time for work shows which professional trait?
r: Reliability
Being on time shows others can count on you.
w: Authority
Punctuality does not give someone authority.
Competitiveness
Punctuality is not about competing.
Creativity
This is a separate trait.

q: Which statement describes why an organization exists and what it does?
r: Mission statement
A mission statement states an organization's purpose.
w: Balance sheet
This lists assets, liabilities and equity.
Job description
This describes one position.
Sales forecast
This estimates future sales.

q: A SWOT analysis examines which four factors?
r: Strengths, weaknesses, opportunities and threats
SWOT stands for these four factors.
w: Sales, wages, output and taxes
These are business measures, not the SWOT factors.
Suppliers, workers, owners and tools
These are resources, not the SWOT factors.
Standards, wants, objectives and targets
These are unrelated planning words.

q: In a SWOT analysis, which item would be listed as a threat?
r: A new competitor opening nearby
Threats are outside forces that could hurt the business.
w: A skilled and loyal staff
This is an internal strength.
An outdated checkout system
This is an internal weakness.
Growing demand for the product
This is an external opportunity.

q: Which growth strategy involves selling existing products in new markets?
r: Market development
Market development takes current products to new customer groups or regions.
w: Market penetration
This sells more of existing products in existing markets.
Product development
This offers new products in existing markets.
Diversification
This offers new products in new markets.

q: Which of the following is a measurable business goal?
r: Increase online sales by 10 percent within six months
It has a number and a deadline, so progress can be tracked.
w: Be the best company in town
This cannot be measured.
Make customers happy
This has no way to show success.
Grow as much as possible
There is no target or time frame.
